result.title: GeoCloak: An Agentic Framework for Semantics-Preserving Geolocation Privacy via Peripheral Clue Manipulation
result.summary: The rapid advancement of large vision language models (LVLMs) has made geolocation inference from images highly accurate and accessible. This poses serious privacy risks: a passive adversary with black-box LVLM access can infer a user's location from a single photo with no metadata. Existing protection methods rely almost exclusively on adversarial perturbation, which introduces perceptible visual artifacts and utility degradation. We identify the visual-geolocation asymmetry: geolocation-decisive clues, such as street signs, tend to be visually peripheral but dominate location inference. Exploiting this asymmetry, we propose GeoCloak, an agentic framework for semantics-preserving geolocation privacy protection. It acts as a clue-aware planner that analyzes each image to identify geolocation-relevant clues, dispatches targeted semantic edits to directly suppress peripheral clues, and autonomously configures adversarial perturbation to further suppress residual geolocation features, all under iterative utility-aware feedback. We evaluate GeoCloak on four diverse datasets spanning 108 countries and 576 cities against five LVLMs and three inference methods. GeoCloak reduces overall city-level accuracy from 41.2% to 9.9%, approximately half of the best-performing baseline, while achieving substantially superior utility preservation both qualitatively and quantitatively. We hope this work takes a meaningful step toward practical, semantics-preserving geolocation privacy protection, giving users greater control over the location information inadvertently embedded in their shared images.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 GeoCloak，一个 agentic 框架：分析图像识别地理位置相关线索，对「视觉上边缘但具决定性」的线索施加定向语义编辑，并自动配置对抗扰动，在效用反馈下迭代抑制 LVLM 的地理定位推断，跨四个数据集与五个 LVLM 评测隐私保护效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「视觉—地理不对称」诊断与按线索定位、抑制视觉证据的规划机制，可能与 LVR 关注的视觉证据筛选、不同区域对模型输出的贡献分配及视觉旁路问题有概念联系，可供核查；但该文面向隐私防御，并非 latent 推理或推理状态生成研究。
